correctness.rationale: For r>=3 positive part sizes, an induced subset avoids a non-induced P4 exactly when it belongs to: a single part; two parts with the smaller occupied count one; or <=3 parts each with one vertex. This proves PF4= T union F_i with T the 2-skeleton of the join of discrete part sets and F_i=Delta(V_i)*D(V\V_i). Pairwise F_i intersections are in T. F_i is contractible and B_i=F_i cap T is K_{n_i,N-n_i}, connected graph with H1 rank (n_i-1)(N-n_i-1). The join is simply connected for r>=3, so its 2-skeleton and all attachments remain simply connected. Integral Mayer-Vietoris splits free H2 extensions and kills all other positive homology; summing ranks gives e2+e3-(r-1)(N-1). Hurewicz + simply connected homology Whitehead identifies a wedge of that many 2-spheres. New independent direct P4 search agrees with face occupancy over six representative part tuples and 792 subset tests. Infinite-family proof algebraic/topological, not based on bounded tests.

originality.rationale: Qualified best-of-knowledge PASS. Deshpande–Goyal–Sawant 2607.05358 provide a general occupancy decomposition, known bipartite PF4, multipartite PF3 and a general wedge conjecture. Their full multipartite r>=3 PF4 homotopy formula was not identified in accessible material; full primary publisher text not obtained, so this is a priority risk, not automatic rejection. Deshpande–Singh higher-independence complex is different from P4-free (four-vertex star is allowed here).
residual_risks: Full text of highly relevant arxiv:2607.05358 was not inspected; explicit previously stated t=4 corollary could alter novelty. This risk alone does not establish prior coverage.
A general decomposition must not be conflated with a homotopy classification; the proof supplies intersection and integral splitting.
